title: Sales Enablement Prospect Pack — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Michael Chen
body:
Overview

This prospect pack is a single, shareable reference for sales and pre-sales teams to present Redwood Inference to engineering and product decision-makers. It combines concise positioning and messaging, competitive brief talking points, a pitch-deck summary with recommended slide order, pricing guidance and example TCO, two short customer case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this document for SDR handoffs, AE presentations, and technical discovery prep.

1) Core positioning (30-second and 2-minute)

- 30-second elevator: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes production LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — lowering latency and unit cost while giving teams the controls they need for reliability and compliance.

- 2-minute value story: Engineering teams choose Redwood when they need consistency between prototypes and production. Our high-throughput runtime, automatic caching and batching, and model/version routing let teams control latency and cost without rebuilding the serving stack. For regulated or large accounts, Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments provide reserved capacity and customer-managed networking with enterprise SLAs. The result: faster time-to-value, repeatable performance, and lower operational risk than ad-hoc self-hosting or black-box APIs.

2) Messaging framework (by buyer persona)

- Platform / Infrastructure (VP/Director level): Emphasize predictable SLOs, capacity commitments (Dedicated), observability (per-route latency/cost), and integration with existing infra (VPC, KMS, SSO). Focus on SLA options and cost predictability for budget planning.

- ML Engineer / MLOps: Emphasize runtime performance (KV cache, continuous batching), model catalog with verified performance profiles, quantization recommendations, and CI/CD-friendly model rollouts (canary / A/B / automatic fallback). Provide benchmark artifacts and perf profiles.

- Product / Engineering Manager: Emphasize developer DX—simple API/SDK, structured outputs, function calling, and predictable latency for user-facing experiences. Use customer stories showing shipped features and time to production.

3) Competitive brief (key competitors and counters)

- General cloud ML endpoints (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI):
  - Strength: integrated cloud ecosystem and infra procurement.
  - Redwood counter: We focus exclusively on inference economics and developer ergonomics across deployment modes; our runtime extracts better cost/latency for transformer workloads via attention optimizations, KV caching, and model routing. For customers requiring multi-cloud portability, Redwood's deployment abstraction and Private options reduce lock-in risk.

- LLM API providers (hosted vendors):
  - Strength: very low friction for prototyping and standard API features.
  - Redwood counter: We match developer ergonomics while providing Dedicated/Private deployment options, clearer unit economics, and production observability designed for scale (token-level cost, per-route dashboards, rollouts).

- Self-hosted inference runtimes (open source runtimes + in-house ops):
  - Strength: ultimate control and potentially lower raw compute costs at scale.
  - Redwood counter: We provide the same control plus an orchestration and observability layer that removes heavy operational burden (autoscaling policies, canary rollouts, KV cache management, and regression alerts tied to evals). Our Dedicated contracts also give predictable throughput and capacity SLAs.

4) Recommended pitch deck (10-12 slides, order and talking points)

Slide 1 — Title + hook: 1-line positioning + customer logo bar.
Slide 2 — The problem: inconsistent latency/cost and runbook drift between prototype and production. Data point: 35-60% variance in per-token cost across custom self-hosted projects (internal benchmark).
Slide 3 — Redwood solution (high level): unified runtime + deployment abstraction.
Slide 4 — Key features: hosted API, Dedicated, Private; caching/batching; rollouts and observability.
Slide 5 — Performance: representative benchmarks (tokens/sec, median p95 latency) vs competitors — include model names and sequence lengths.
Slide 6 — Reliability & SLAs: uptime targets, fallbacks, and error budgets.
Slide 7 — Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO checklist (prospect summary).
Slide 8 — Pricing & TCO: example committed capacity vs pay-as-you-go comparison (see Pricing Guidance table).
Slide 9 — Case studies: two short success stories with outcomes (latency reduced, cost per 1M tokens).
Slide 10 — Rollout plan: pilot → integration → production → scale (owner, success criteria, timeline).
Slide 11 — Next steps & ask: pilot proposal and technical discovery checklist.
Slide 12 — Appendix / technical contacts and benchmark artifacts link.

5) Pricing guidance and example TCO (sales playbook level)

- Pricing pillars: Hosted (usage-based), Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity + overage), Private (platform license + support).

- Typical starter offers to propose during early conversations:
  1) Self-serve trial: free credits and standard hosted API access (no SLA).
  2) Pilot package (recommended): 3 month pilot on hosted with 50% committed capacity discount + evaluation dashboard and one integration workshop (SRE/ML lead).
  3) Dedicated POC: 6 month reserved node commitment at reduced hourly rate, includes 1 performance onboarding session + 30 days of enhanced observability retention.

- Example TCO table (simplified) — use when building a prospect quote:

  Scenario | Monthly tokens | Unit price (hosted) | Monthly cost (hosted) | Dedicated equivalent (monthly commit)
  ---------|----------------|--------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------
  A: Prototype | 50M tokens | $0.0008 / token | $40,000 | n/a
  B: Early production | 500M tokens | $0.0006 / token | $300,000 | $26,000 (reserved pool amortized)
  C: Scale | 5B tokens | $0.00035 / token | $1,750,000 | $220,000 (reserved + burst)

- Pricing play: emphasize breakpoints where Dedicated becomes cost-effective (rough rule: committed capacity when >~200-300M tokens/month depending on model mix and latency SLOs). Always include observability and rollout professional services in the pilot proposal for enterprise deals.

6) Two short case studies (one SaaS, one Enterprise)

Case study 1 — SaaS search provider (PLG growth):
- Challenge: inconsistent search response latency and high token costs during bursts.
- Solution: Migrated ranking and fast-path completions to Redwood Dedicated; enabled prefix caching for frequent queries and autoscaling for burst windows.
- Outcome: 45% reduction in median latency for search completions (from 160ms to 88ms), 38% reduction in per-token cost vs prior managed endpoint, and 3 week time-to-production.

Case study 2 — Regulated financial analytics platform (Enterprise, private deployment):
- Challenge: data residency and auditability requirements prevented use of third-party hosted-only APIs.
- Solution: Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC, KMS integration, and dedicated capacity for inference workloads.
- Outcome: Achieved SOC-equivalent audit evidence for model inference pipelines, met regional data residency SLA, and stabilized monthly inference spend with a 12-month reserved contract.

7) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for common questions)

Q: Where is data stored, and how long is it retained?
A: Hosted API: request/response payloads are retained by default for 30 days for debugging and billing reconciliation; retention can be configured and reduced to 0 days on request for certain enterprise customers. Dedicated/Private: customers control retention via config and KMS policies; Redwood retains only metadata required for billing (subject to contract).

Q: Do you support customer KMS/HSM and managed keys?
A: Yes. Redwood supports customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private, with HSM integrations for vaulting keys in compliance-sensitive environments.

Q: Can we deploy in our VPC / air-gapped environment?
A: Private deployment options include VPC-integrated managed control plane and an on-prem package for air-gapped installs. We provide an ops runbook and an onboarding engagement for installation and hardening.

Q: What compliance certifications or evidence do you provide?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II readiness artifacts and ISO-aligned controls. For enterprise deals we provide a compliance evidence package and support for customer audits. Specific attestation copies are shared under NDA.

Q: How is access controlled and audited?
A: Role-based access control (RBAC), SSO (SAML/OIDC), and per-token audit logging are standard. Audit logs are exportable to customer SIEMs for long-term retention.

Q: How do you handle model and output safety (PII, toxic content)?
A: We provide model onboarding guardrails, evaluation harnesses, and policy hooks to run custom filters. Redwood also supports prompt/eval-based regression alerts tied to upstream CI so teams can catch model drift before rollout.

8) Technical discovery checklist (what to gather before a pilot)

- Workload profile: expected tokens/month, peak qps, typical sequence lengths, and latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets).
- Model requirements: preferred model(s), need for quantized variants, custom model upload.
- Security & compliance: data residency, KMS/HSM requirements, SSO provider, audit retention window.
- Integration points: desired observability exports (Datadog/Prometheus/CloudWatch), routing policies, and storage/PVC requirements for Private.
- Success criteria and timeline: pilot acceptance metrics, owner, and target date to move to Dedicated/Private.

9) Enablement assets and playbooks (links and recommended usage)

- Pitch deck artifacts: slide deck (editable), benchmark workbook (CSV with p50/p95/token throughput), and sample code snippets for quick start.
- Demo scripts: two demo flows (search completion and chat assistant) with expected latency metrics and test datasets.
- Sales scripts: objection handlers for cost, security, and vendor lock-in (short bullets for SDR/AEs).

Appendix: Links to benchmarks, onboarding runbooks, and legal templates will be attached to the editable deck.
